See its really hard to say honestly. Because most people when they get into a fight until they have done it a couple times and trained some everything they ever heard is gonna go right our the window and they are just gonna do what feels natural to them. There's no shortcut to learning how to fight. There are some basic techniques tho that are good to keep in mind. Honestly tho. I feel a lot if not most street fights wind up on the ground so I would probly try to show some basic grappling as well instead of just boxing like maybe some takedown defense, or a couple lil simple hand fighting and tying up techniques(rolling the wrist to break the grip, grabbing above the elbow, head control) and basic stand up maneuvers. But boxing wise keeping ur chin down when u throw is a good idea (like he said in the video), keep ur hands up, I always tell new people 1 punch at a time. People tend to get excited and try to throw a flurry that winds up with both their hands outstretched. One hand always protects the other throws. Don't start ur 2nd punch til ur 1st has returned to its proper defensive position. Easier remembered as 1 punch at a time. Always keep ur eyes open. You would be surprised how many people completely shut their eyes when swinging. Don't do that. Always keep ur eyes on the target. This way even if ur gonna get hit u can at leaSt see it coming. If ur gonna tie up up high (grab each other on upper half of body) keep ur butt back to keep ur weigh back. Learn a sprawl. This is getting lengthy and I apologize. I honestly wish I could remember the video a lil better so I could.maybe give my critiques or alternate techniques to what he's saying. But I just remember not really liking his basics. I thought it was things that aren't really gonna help a newbie In a fight. I mean anything u tell them to do is gonna be done sloppy so u have to keep it simple easy to remember and still be effective. So idk. I feel like there really is no 3 basic steps or 10 techniques or any set number or basic set of stuff u could tell some one. Fighting is too complex theirs too many aspects to it and every body has their own opinion on what's best. It's hard to pick a few basics that are good for everyone to know in all situations. I would say if ur really worried at learning the basics. Learn how to properly throw a series of punches. Anyone can throw 1 punch (most can even throw 1 good one) but stringing then together is hard and it's usually the 2 or 3 punch that actually Lands. So I would learn a simple combo u can throw like 1-2-3 or 1-2-3-4 or 2-3-2 or 2-3-2-4. Then learn the basics on the different positions of being on the ground. U might not become a master at being in guard or side control or whatever but knowing how do identify the positions so u can identify when ur in one is good to know. Basic ways to stand back up when u hit the ground basic ways to hold onto people and how to properly grip ur hands. Then maybe a basic submission like a rear naked choke.
